entities.summary: Benedict VII was a Roman Catholic Pope from 985 to 983, succeeding Pope John XVII and being succeeded by Pope John XVIII. He played a significant role in the ecclesiastical politics of the late 10th century, navigating the complex relationships between the Holy Roman Empire and the Papal States. Benedict VII was a key figure in the Papal States' efforts to consolidate their power and influence in the region. His papacy was marked by several significant events, including the attempted deposition of the Pope by the Holy Roman Emperor Otto II and the recognition of the authority of the Patriarch of Constantinople. The legacy of Benedict VII can be seen in the continued influence of the Papal States on the politics of the region and the development of the concept of papal infallibility. The Benedictine monk and theologian, Gerhoh of Reichersberg, wrote a biography of Benedict VII, providing valuable insights into the life and reign of the Pope. In his biography, Gerhoh portrayed Benedict VII as a wise and learned leader who navigated the treacherous waters of ecclesiastical politics with skill and diplomacy. The papacy of Benedict VII also saw the rise of the Benedictine Order as a major force in the region, with the Pope playing a key role in the promotion of monastic life and spirituality. The papacy of Benedict VII was marked by several significant events, including the coronation of the Holy Roman Emperor Otto III and the recognition of the authority of the Patriarch of Constantinople.
